items.answer: observation

items.stem:
Read the extract.

In March 2020 supermarket sales of toilet paper in many countries more than doubled for several weeks as shoppers stockpiled.

Define the term "seasonal variation". [2]
items.answer: The difference between actual sales and the trend that recurs at the same time each year
items.markingKey: [2] for a full, accurate definition: the difference between actual sales and the trend that recurs at the same time each year. [1] for a partial definition. Examples alone are not credited.

items.stem: A population is 60% female. In a stratified sample of 200, the number of females should be:
Alessia writes: "Quantitative research is always more reliable than qualitative research." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Numbers can come from biased samples or poor questions; qualitative research can reveal motives that numbers miss.
items.markingKey: Numbers can come from biased samples or poor questions; qualitative research can reveal motives that numbers miss. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Read the extract.

Lego's researchers observed girls playing in the late 2000s before launching Lego Friends in 2012, which became one of its best-selling ranges.

Explain why a business might use secondary research before primary research. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: It is cheaper and quicker, gives an overview of the market and helps identify what specific questions primary research needs to answer.

items.stem:
Read the extract.

Zara uses daily sales data from its stores to adjust production in short runs, rather than relying on long-term forecasts.

Explain why moving averages are used to identify the trend. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Averaging consecutive periods smooths out seasonal and random fluctuations, so the underlying direction of sales becomes clearer.

items.stem: Explain why convenience sampling may give biased results.
items.answer: People who are easy to reach, such as passers-by at one time and place, may not represent the whole target market, so their views can be skewed.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: People who are easy to reach, such as passers-by at one time and place, may not represent the whole target market, so their views can be skewed. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between qualitative research and quantitative research.
items.answer: Qualitative research collects in-depth views and reasons from small groups; quantitative research collects numerical data from larger samples that can be analysed statistically.
items.markingKey: Qualitative research collects in-depth views and reasons from small groups; quantitative research collects numerical data from larger samples that can be analysed statistically. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between a focus group and a questionnaire.
items.answer: A focus group gives in-depth qualitative views from a few people; a questionnaire collects mainly quantitative data from many respondents.
items.markingKey: A focus group gives in-depth qualitative views from a few people; a questionnaire collects mainly quantitative data from many respondents. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Café Andino's annual sales (thousand units) were: 2019 86, 2020 58, 2021 76, 2022 40, 2023 50. Calculate the three-year moving averages.
items.markingKey: (86 + 58 + 76)/3 = 73.3; (58 + 76 + 40)/3 = 58.0; (76 + 40 + 50)/3 = 55.3 [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for all three averages, centred on the middle year. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: "A larger sample always produces accurate results." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Size reduces random sampling error, but a biased method (e.g. surveying only one location) gives misleading results however large the sample.
items.markingKey: Size reduces random sampling error, but a biased method (e.g. surveying only one location) gives misleading results however large the sample. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. asked 11 customers to rate a new product from 1 to 10. Scores: 3, 10, 4, 2, 2, 9, 9, 6, 10, 8, 7. Calculate the mean, median, mode and range of the scores.
items.answer: Mean = 70/11 = 6.36; median = 7; mode = 2, 9 and 10 (multimodal); range = 10 − 2 = 8.
items.markingKey: ordered: 2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 10, 10; mean = total/number; median = middle value; mode = most frequent; range = highest − lowest. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for all four statistics. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: A start-up café plans to open near a university. Suggest one primary and one secondary research method it should use and explain what each would reveal.
items.answer: Primary: a survey or observation of students near the site, showing prices they will pay and preferred products. Secondary: council data on student numbers and footfall, or competitor menus online, showing market size and competition.
items.markingKey: Primary: a survey or observation of students near the site, showing prices they will pay and preferred products. Secondary: council data on student numbers and footfall, or competitor menus online, showing market size and competition.

items.stem: Outline one way in which retail sales in December shows seasonal variation.
items.answer: UK retailers typically make a large share of annual sales in November and December, around Black Friday and Christmas. Firms hire temporary staff and build stock before the seasonal peak
